quote: 2.6. Stochastic ordering. Theorem 5. Let S∼ CD(η_1, ϕ_1) and Q∼ CD(η_2, ϕ_2). If η_1 = η_2 and ϕ_1 = ϕ_2 and ϕ_1 ≥ ϕ_2 (or if ϕ_2 = ϕ_2 and η_1 = η_2 and η_1 ≥ η_2), then S ≤_stor Q and hence S ≤_Ror Q, S ≤_mrl Q and S ≤_lor Q.
family: Remkan distribution: three-component mixture of exponential(η), gamma(3, η) and gamma(4, η) with mixing proportions τ_1 = η/(η+2ϕ+6), τ_2 = 2ϕ/(η+2ϕ+6), τ_3 = 6/(η+2ϕ+6); pdf (3) g(x; η, ϕ) = η^2/(η+2ϕ+6) [1 + ϕηx^2 + η^2x^3] e^{−ηx}; x > 0, η > 0, ϕ > 0; cdf (4) as printed G(x; η, ϕ) = 1 − [1 + (η^3x^3 + (3+ϕ)η^2x^3 + (6+2ϕ)ηx)/(η+2ϕ+6)] e^{−ηx}; survival (30) as printed s(x) = [1 + (η^3x^3 + (3+ϕ)η^2x^3 + (6+2ϕ)ηx)/(η+2ϕ+6)] e^{−ηx}
compared: parameters (η_1, ϕ_1) of S vs (η_2, ϕ_2) of Q, under the printed conditions

hypotheses.text: Let S∼ CD(η_1, ϕ_1) and Q∼ CD(η_2, ϕ_2)
hypotheses.formal: S and Q have pdf (3) with parameters (η_1, ϕ_1) and (η_2, ϕ_2) respectively (CD read as the paper's Remkan distribution)
η_1, η_2 > 0; ϕ_1, ϕ_2 > 0; support x > 0

hypotheses.text: If η_1 = η_2 and ϕ_1 = ϕ_2 and ϕ_1 ≥ ϕ_2
hypotheses.formal: as printed: η_1 = η_2 and ϕ_1 = ϕ_2, so ϕ_1 ≥ ϕ_2 is implied and S, Q are identically distributed

hypotheses.text: (or if ϕ_2 = ϕ_2 and η_1 = η_2 and η_1 ≥ η_2)
hypotheses.formal: as printed: ϕ_2 = ϕ_2 is vacuous and η_1 = η_2 implies η_1 ≥ η_2, so this alternative reads η_1 = η_2 with ϕ_1, ϕ_2 unrestricted

quantifiers: all x > 0; η_i > 0, ϕ_i > 0 subject to the printed conditions
ambiguity: The printed conditions are degenerate: the first alternative forces η_1 = η_2 and ϕ_1 = ϕ_2 (identical distributions), and the second contains the tautology 'ϕ_2 = ϕ_2' plus η_1 = η_2, which makes 'η_1 ≥ η_2' redundant. The intended conditions cannot be recovered from the text. '≤_stor' is never defined; the sentence after the proof writes '≤_sor', and 'stochastic orderings' is the only gloss. 'CD(η, ϕ)' is never defined (the paper studies the Remkan distribution; the reference list includes the Copoun distribution). The printed cdf (4) and survival (30) contain the term (3+ϕ)η^2x^3, whereas the quantile function (10)/(14) has (3+ϕ)η^2x_q^2, so the printed forms conflict. Eq. (1) writes τ_2 g_3 (τ_2 twice), and the introduction first defines a second 'τ_2 = 6/(η+2ϕ+6)'. Proof eq. (37) gives f_S/f_Q = η_1^2(η_2+ϕ_2+6)/(η_2^2(η_1+2ϕ_1+6)) · e^{−(η_1−η_2)φ}, omitting the factor [1 + ϕηφ^2 + η^2φ^3] of pdf (3) and printing (η_2+ϕ_2+6) rather than (η_2+2ϕ_2+6). No stochastic-order definitions appear anywhere in the paper. Page 10 is the image index; the printed page is 342.

quantifiers: all x > 0; η_i > 0, ϕ_i > 0 subject to the printed conditions
ambiguity: '≤_Ror' is never defined. Its reading as the hazard rate order rests on the paper calling the hazard function the 'risk measurement function' (Section 2.5.2) and on the post-proof sentence ('... has risk measurement, average residual measurement life, and stochastic orderings'). The theorem says this order follows 'hence' from ≤_stor, while the post-proof sentence gives the chain S ≤_lor Q ⟹ S ≤_Ror Q ⟹ {S ≤_sor Q, S ≤_mrl Q}; the direction of derivation conflicts. The degenerate printed conditions, undefined CD, and formula inconsistencies are as described in the ≤_stor record.

ambiguity: '≤_lor' is never defined. The reading as the likelihood ratio order rests on the post-proof sentence ('the Remkan distribution is ordered in the likelihood ratio'). The proof works with log(f_S/f_Q) via eqs. (37)–(39), where d/dφ log(f_S/f_Q) = −(η_2 − η_1), but it does not state which sign or monotonicity defines ≤_lor. The ratio (37) omits the polynomial factor [1 + ϕηφ^2 + η^2φ^3] of pdf (3). The theorem derives ≤_lor 'hence' from ≤_stor, whereas the post-proof chain starts from ≤_lor. The degenerate printed conditions and undefined CD are as described in the ≤_stor record.
